population.note: Four chapters so far (Region and Regional Development; Geography: Nature and Scope; Population: Part 2; Population: Part 1), 2026-09-24. RECALL IS UNMEASURABLE FOR THIS LANE AND THE PROBE SAYS SO ('n/a'): no chapter yet has an attached figure, so there is no known-positive population to measure the rule against and the flagged count is a FLOOR rather than a count. All 33 hits are SELFCONTAINED, and that is a property of THIS BOOK'S GRAPHICS rather than luck. Every one of them is a concept map, a skill chart, a job advertisement, a pictogram, a labelled bar or pie chart, or a shape-only population pyramid - text, labelled numbers, or shape. None is an image a reader must measure, so a transcription can inline it completely, and these do. The weakest case is Population Part 1's fig. 1.5, a pair of satellite rasters where the student must take the chapter's own reading on trust; it is recorded as SELFCONTAINED because the chapter states the conclusion in prose, but it is the one row here that would genuinely be better with the image. THE PROBE READS `context`, NOT ONLY `text`: most of these rows have stems with no figure word in them at all ('Which region has the highest literacy rate?', 'What does the image show?') and were flagged through the shared set context. This will stop being true for the chapters that follow. Ch.4, Ch.5 and Ch.6 carry 'On an outline map of the world, show the following' questions (DRAWS, not MISS), and Ch.3, Ch.5 and Ch.6 carry 'study the map/figure above and answer' questions over real choropleths, which are genuine MISS candidates until a figure is attached.

rows.why: 'Go through the Regional Imbalance Reduction Strategy chart (fig. 7.2) and write two sentences on each factor' keeps the book's figure citation, but the chart's ENTIRE content is reproduced in the stem directly beneath it: both branches (Provision of Public Goods/Services, Provision of Infrastructure and Stimulus) and all eleven leaf factors, transcribed off the rendered page. Fig. 7.2 is a concept map, not a data graphic - it carries no values, no scale and no legend, so the labels ARE the figure. A student can answer it in full from the text alone. This is the class the probe's own 26% measured precision is made of: a figure CITATION is not a figure DEPENDENCE. The citation was deliberately kept rather than stripped, because it is the row's provenance back to the printed page, and stripping it would change the stem and therefore the content_hash of an already-committed row.

'Make a list of the skills obtained through the study of Geography ... (fig. 8.1, Skills of a Geographer)' keeps the citation, and the stem then lists all nine skills the figure contains. Fig. 8.1 is a labelled spider chart with no data, no scale and no picture - its labels ARE its content, and they are reproduced verbatim. Answerable in full from the text.

'A newspaper item listing job opportunities is given below (fig. 8.5, Sample Advertisement)' - all seven advertisements are transcribed into the stem, each with its post, qualifications, experience and post count. Fig. 8.5 is a rasterised clipping of TEXT, so nothing is lost by inlining it. Note this figure is also the reason the chapter needs a figtext.json: its glyphs carry the +29 cmap offset documented in config.ts, so the text layer renders it as '8QLRQ3XEOLF6HUYLFH' and it had to be read off the rendered page.
